thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — high error rate detected for customer 'Semaphore Labs' (private VPC). Affected: egress to analytics partner (10.64.33.0/24). Error spike started ~1777777700. Auto-alert: NLB target unhealthy + DNS failures. Paging ops-oncall and net-oncall.
Marcos: oncall ack — I'm up, grabbing logs and NLB health.
Jena: net-oncall here, joining. seeing a flood of TIME_WAIT+SYN_RECV on the tenant NAT instances, conntrack near capacity. likely conntrack exhaustion causing new connections to drop; NLB healthchecks also failing intermittently.
Olivia: support — customer reports 503s for outbound webhook deliveries since ~09:12 UTC, some retries succeed. They say ~25% of webhooks delayed >30s.
Ravi: AE — I'm on the customer call, they want ETA and if we can route around the problem. They mentioned this tenant uses Dedicated Private pool + VPC egress via our managed NAT instances behind an NLB.
Kyle: infra — if conntrack is saturated on the NAT hosts, we can either scale NAT hosts or temporarily shift traffic off the affected instances via NLB target deregistration/drain. Also we can lower Route53 TTL and shift weighted routing to a standby egress pool.
Marcos: confirmed conntrack stats. snippet from the NAT-01 host:
```
# conntrack -S
# nf_conntrack: used 131072 entries, peak 131500, size 131072
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
131072
```
Jena: net note — the tenant's flow pattern changed (bursty retries). default nf_conntrack_max too small for this tenant's bursty egress + long-lived sockets.
Olivia: customer on call: "This is impacting critical deliveries to our partner. Can you stop the failures now?"
Marcos: quick mitigation plan: 1) spin new NAT host(s) into dedicated pool 2) drain unhealthy NAT instances from NLB (target deregister) 3) lower Route53 TTL for customer CNAME so we can shift weighting if needed 4) increase conntrack on existing hosts as short-term patch.
Jena: I'll increase conntrack on the two most impacted NATs now (temporary). running:
```sh
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```
Jena: applying the sysctl change — will monitor.
Marcos: while that's in flight, Kyle, can you provision one extra NAT host in the Semaphore private pool and register it behind the NLB? Keep healthcheck strict (30s) and put it into draining/standby until we see green.
Kyle: provisioning new-nat-03 (t3a.medium equiv). Registering with NLB target group tg-semaphore-egress:
```sh
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elbv2:...:tg-semaphore-egress --targets Id=i-0abcd1234efgh5678
```
Kyle: target registered. healthchecks are starting. will wait for healthy -> then we can shift weights by deregistering unhealthy ones.
Ravi: customer update draft: "We're actively mitigating a networking resource exhaustion that affected outbound traffic to one of your partners. We're adding capacity and performing temporary routing changes to restore delivery. Expect partial recovery in the next 10-20 minutes." Agree?
Olivia: yep send that. keep tone: precise and not too technical. say "we're not changing payloads". add contact for status updates.
Marcos: Jena, what does netstat look like now?
Jena: conntrack count down to 83k after sysctl bump + some retries cleared. NLB still shows 2/4 targets unhealthy (the ones with sustained high conntrack). new-nat-03 health is PASSING.
Marcos: OK — start draining the two suspect NAT instances from NLB to cut incoming new connections:
```sh
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elbv2:...:tg-semaphore-egress --targets Id=i-0badcafe12345678 Id=i-0feedface87654321
```
Marcos: deregistered. we expect ~60s for connection draining to complete.
Jena: lowering customer Route53 TTL from 300 to 30 to allow faster cutover if we need DNS-based failover. applied change:
```json
{"ChangeBatch": {"Changes": [{"Action": "UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "egress.semaphore.example","Type": "CNAME","TTL": 30,"ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "egress-pool-a.example."}]}}]}}
```
Marcos: monitoring customer webhook success rate. metrics show error rate down from 24% -> 6% since draining started. latency also improving.
Ravi: customer asked: any possibility of data loss?
Olivia: retries are in place and partner returns 2xx for retried deliveries. no evidence of permanent loss; deliveries are delayed. we'll confirm post-incident.
Kyle: new-nat-03 now healthy and serving. post-drain count on bad NATs shows connections draining to 0. Consider increasing autoscale policy for the dedicated pool to avoid future manual provisioning.
Jena: adding a short-lived conntrack autoscaling doc item to runbook: if nf_conntrack > 80% for 2m, auto-provision + temp-increase nf_conntrack_max.
Marcos: coordinating a controlled rollback plan in case shifting breaks anything: we can re-register targets and restore previous TTL (300) for DNS.
Ravi: customer on call says they see failed rate dropping. asking for a timeline on root cause fix.
Marcos: root cause hypothesis: tenant had a sudden retry storm combined with existing long-lived flows, overwhelming conntrack on managed NAT hosts. Secondary effect: NLB healthchecks failing when NAT cannot establish outbound probes. Action items: short-term config bump (done), add capacity (done), long-term: tune conntrack autoscaling + telemetry per-tenant, limit long-lived connection retention for dedicated pools.
Olivia: I'll send post-incident initial note to the customer: short summary + mitigation + ETA for follow-up RCA in 24h. Ravi, can you review before I send?
Ravi: reviewing now. :thumbsup:
Marcos: quick housekeeping: please add the following to the incident ticket: impacted tenant id: TEN-4387, peak error rate 24%, affected partner IP range 10.64.33.0/24, mitigation steps (conntrack bump, added nat host, drained unhealthy targets, lowered TTL), owner: Marcos (SRE), net owner: Jena.
Jena: logging: pushed sysctl changes and monitoring graphs to the incident doc. I'll schedule a follow-up to propose permanent fixes: conntrack autoscale + per-tenant egress quotas.
Kyle: infra action: create a playbook change to add a healthcheck-weighted target shift for future incidents and a terraform change to add a small buffer pool for tenant-dedicated NATs.
Marcos: thanks team. Incident currently in "mitigated" state, continuing to observe for 30m. Will update thread when we close. :white_check_mark:
Olivia: sent the customer note, included our contact and a quick status timeline.
Ravi: customer ended call appreciative of speed. will want a formal RCA and timeline for the long-term fix.
Marcos: final update: 30m observation window passed, error rate stable at <1.5%. closing incident to 'resolved-will-commit-rca'. assigning follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (1777777777). Please file RCA within 48h and link to ticket INC-2026-5823.
Marcos: filing RCA now. thanks all. :party_parrot:
